summary.text: A daughter of Sthenelus son of Perseus and of Nicippe daughter of Pelops — sister to Medusa and to Eurystheus in the Perseid house at Mycenae before the birth-contest that gave the kingdom to her younger brother.

Homonym guard: not Alcyone daughter of Aeolus (`alcyone-aeolid`); not the Pleiad (`alcyone-pleiad`); not Alcyone daughter of Atlas in the Ceyx tale. This Alcyone belongs only to Sthenelus' Mycenaean brood.

story.text: Apollodorus names Alcyone and Medusa as the two daughters Sthenelus begot upon Nicippe before the son Eurystheus, who reigned over Mycenae when the Perseid line still held the fortress. She stands in the generation between Perseus' founding sons and the lord who imposed the Labours on Heracles.
